question: Which renewal looks most at risk, and why?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract every statement from this call that signals the customer's likelihood to renew or churn: expressed dissatisfaction, complaints, unresolved issues, usage or adoption levels, budget or pricing pressure, competitor mentions or evaluations, stakeholder changes, contract or renewal terms discussed, and any explicit statements about continuing, reducing, or cancelling. Include the speaker and quote the relevant wording, and note whether OrbitFlow staff responded or resolved each concern.
assumptions: 'Renewal' interpreted as the Renewal call type (CALL-011, CALL-012, CALL-013), since the question asks which renewal looks at risk.
Risk judgement must be made by comparing findings across the renewal calls, so each call is read for underlying risk signals rather than a verdict.

findings.speaker: Devan Shah
findings.quote: Resolution times on anything involving the SAP connector have been terrible. We had a ticket open for nineteen days in July.
findings.context: Customer reports SAP connector ticket resolution has been terrible; a ticket sat for eleven days and fell between teams. Vendor acknowledged, offered a named escalation contact but no resolution SLA. — Unresolved support issue (resolution times, not response times); vendor partially responded with named engineer, declined SLA

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Resolution-time commitments are a different thing and we don't do them.
findings.context: Customer asked whether the SAP escalation issue could be addressed in the contract; vendor said resolution-time commitments are not offered. — Vendor declined contractual resolution commitment; customer noted it

findings.speaker: Devan Shah
findings.quote: Because from our side we did nothing wrong and it cost us twenty thousand runs.
findings.context: Run volume exceeded contracted tier in four of six months, and the March retry storm cost the customer about 20,000 runs; customer questioned whether it would recur. Vendor said retry configuration is partly the customer's responsibility and scheduled a session. — Overage/cost friction; vendor took partial responsibility and committed to a configuration session

findings.speaker: Fiona Bright
findings.quote: That's — okay. That's a more sensible conversation than I was braced for.
findings.context: Customer says nine licensed builders with four dormant is a problem; vendor proposed reducing to seven seats, which the customer accepted as more reasonable than expected. — Seat reduction is a downgrade signal; framed by vendor as a genuine reduction, not an upsell

findings.speaker: Fiona Bright
findings.quote: Nine percent for forty percent more capacity and a new use case.
findings.context: Customer expected a 15% uplift and was relieved by the 7% list uplift; total projected to rise about 9% with seat reduction and a 400k tier. — Pricing pressure; customer relieved relative to expectation, but finance review required

findings.speaker: Fiona Bright
findings.quote: It won't slip.
findings.context: Renewal decision will go through a finance director; customer will return the week of the fifteenth and expects it not to slip past the eighteenth October expiry. — Stakeholder approval process and timeline; short six-week window

findings.speaker: Fiona Bright
findings.quote: The depot exception routing. Without question. Everything else we could go back to doing the old way and survive.
findings.context: Customer is strongly positive about core value (depot exception routing and run history), which suggests low churn intent despite friction points. — Counterweight to risk: value is high and embedded in operations

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: Your renewal's on the twenty-ninth of November. Usage has dropped about forty percent since March.
findings.context: Usage has dropped about forty percent since March and the renewal is on 29 November; Ruth raised the at-risk concern directly. — Vendor CSM opening framing of the renewal risk

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: Ravi bought it, Ravi implemented it, Ravi left in February, and I picked it up in March with about forty minutes of handover.
findings.context: Customer inherited the product after the champion left with only forty minutes of handover; the vendor acknowledged its own onboarding failure. — Adoption root cause; vendor accepted fault

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: I'd rather tell you that plainly than imply we're watching when we aren't.
findings.context: Six of fourteen production workflows have not run successfully in 90 days, including a temp workflow failing every four hours since January with alerts going to an unread mailbox; vendor does not proactively monitor at this tier. — Estate health and unresolved failures; vendor admitted gap

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: I don't know. That's the honest answer. The claims director changed in April and the new one has a different view about where triage should happen.
findings.context: Customer is uncertain whether the claims triage reason for buying still holds, as the claims director wants triage moved into Guidewire; the cross-system build is not native. — Core use case at risk; competitor-platform alternative (Guidewire) favoured internally

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: One person uses it. She's brilliant, she's called Ellie, and she's been on maternity leave since June.
findings.context: Only one builder ever worked; the other builders attempted training but it did not take, and the sole builder is on leave until November, so nobody is operating the product. — Adoption and bus-factor risk

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Looking at what you're actually using, I'm not sure you should be.
findings.context: Vendor's Enterprise tier is poorly matched to usage; the Growth tier would drop SSO, which the customer's security standard requires, so no cheaper tier fits. — Pricing/tier pressure; vendor flagged overspend

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: I'm not going to pretend I'm enthusiastic. If you'd asked me two weeks ago I'd have said we're not renewing.
findings.context: Customer is considering not renewing; vendor offered a no-renewal exit and a six-month option with enablement included, and the customer said they would otherwise have not renewed two weeks earlier. — Explicit churn signal and retention offer; customer softened after vendor candour

findings.speaker: Nadia Rahman
findings.quote: Low ticket volume can mean two things.
findings.context: Support tickets are closed by customer without help and responses are within SLA but unhelpful, so low ticket volume may mask dissatisfaction; vendor agreed to be more careful with that metric. — Unresolved support complaint; customer says they stopped raising tickets

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Your current contract auto-renews with sixty days' notice, which means your notice deadline is the thirtieth of September.
findings.context: Customer's current contract auto-renews unless notice is served by 30 September, a deadline the customer did not know; vendor advised serving notice. — Renewal terms and timing risk; vendor surfaced it proactively

findings.speaker: Nadia Rahman
findings.quote: I don't think the product is the problem. I think we implemented it badly, one person owned it
findings.context: Customer's own view is that the product is not the problem and the failure is an internal implementation issue, which is a mitigating factor for retention. — Counterweight to churn risk; attributes problem to Pinewood

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: You're renewing in November, usage is healthy, six builders all active, error rate under one percent, and the only change is a seven percent standard uplift.
findings.context: Customer confirmed the renewal is straightforward and fine; usage healthy with six builders active and only a seven percent standard uplift. — Renewal in November; vendor stated usage metrics and Grace accepted the seven percent uplift as not worth more time. Low churn signal.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: Seven percent on a number that size is not worth an hour of my life.
findings.context: Customer said the seven percent uplift is acceptable and the renewal is fine. — Customer acceptance of price change; no pricing objection raised.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: Renewal is agreed subject to papers — seven percent, no other changes, AI consumption estimate included.
findings.context: Renewal agreed subject to papers at seven percent with no other changes; AI consumption estimate to be included. — Vendor summary at close; customer confirmed it as accurate. Supports a likely renewal, conditional on written papers.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: For four hundred incidents a month it's not material. I'll put a number on it so nobody's surprised, but I don't think it changes your renewal.
findings.context: Customer raised a concern that the consumption element of AI usage may add cost; vendor said it is not material at current volume and does not change renewal. — Possible cost friction on AI consumption; vendor reassured and promised a number in the renewal papers.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: Put the number in anyway.
findings.context: Customer asked for the AI consumption number explicitly to avoid surprises; wants cost visibility. — Customer wants the number included despite vendor saying immaterial.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: Right. I'm supportive, subject to the four written answers.
findings.context: Customer is conditionally supportive of expansion (AI use), subject to written answers and a fifty-incident test; open items may delay expansion but not renewal. — Expansion risk: AI rollout gated on five written answers and a two-week test. Not a churn signal per se.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: It's not a criticism of the product. It's a criticism of us, and slightly of you for not mentioning it eighteen months ago.
findings.context: Vendor's governance remark about no change control was received with discomfort; customer frustration directed at the company's own gap rather than the product. — Customer said worst thing is lack of change control; framed as criticism of themselves and slightly of vendor for not raising it earlier. Mild friction, not product dissatisfaction.

findings.speaker: Tobias Lund
findings.quote: We used to take eleven days to bring a new managed detection client live and now it's four.
findings.context: Customer praised the client onboarding workflow as the best outcome, reducing time-to-live from eleven days to four. — Strong value signal supporting retention.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: Good. Thank you both.
findings.context: Overall the call shows low churn risk: no competitor evaluation, no cancellation or downgrade statements, and cordial tone. — Inferred from absence of churn signals and positive closing tone.

draft.answer: Pinewood Insurance (CALL-012) looks most at risk: usage is down about 40% since March, the customer said it would not have renewed two weeks earlier, and the notice deadline is 30 September [C1][C2][C3]. Lumen Retail Group has friction but is likely to renew, and Halberd Security looks low risk [C4][C5].

claims.text: Pinewood Insurance: Ruth Adeyemi (vendor CSM) said usage has dropped about forty percent since March, with renewal on 29 November. Graham Attwood (Director of Operations) said that two weeks earlier he would have said they were not renewing, and that he is not enthusiastic. The vendor offered a no-renewal exit and a six-month option with enablement included, and he softened after the vendor's candour.

Pinewood adoption and estate problems: the champion (Ravi) left in February with about forty minutes of handover, and the vendor acknowledged its own onboarding failure. Only one builder (Ellie) ever worked, and she is on maternity leave until November, so nobody is operating the product. Six of fourteen production workflows have not run successfully in 90 days, and the vendor does not proactively monitor at this tier.

Pinewood commercial and strategic risks: Graham is uncertain the claims triage use case still holds, because the new claims director wants triage in Guidewire. The Enterprise tier is poorly matched to usage, and the Growth tier would drop SSO, which the customer's security standard requires, so no cheaper tier fits. The contract auto-renews unless notice is served by 30 September, a deadline the customer did not know, and Leo Grant advised serving notice. Nadia Rahman said low ticket volume can mask dissatisfaction because tickets are closed without help.
Mitigating factor at Pinewood: Nadia Rahman said the product is not the problem and the failure was an internal implementation issue with one person owning it.

Lumen Retail Group has friction but appears likely to renew. Devan Shah complained of poor SAP connector resolution times (a ticket open for days), and Maya Chen (vendor) said resolution-time commitments are not offered. Run volume exceeded the tier in four of six months, and a March retry storm cost about 20,000 runs. Fiona Bright was relieved by the 7% uplift (about 9% total with a seat reduction to seven) and called depot exception routing the key value. Finance director approval is needed, and she said the decision will not slip past the 18 October expiry.

Halberd Security looks low risk: Grace Okonkwo accepted the 7% uplift, and renewal was agreed subject to papers with no other changes and an AI consumption estimate included. Open items (AI expansion conditions, her request for the AI consumption number) may delay expansion but not renewal. The call-level low-risk read is inferred.

conflicts.description: Nadia Rahman blames internal implementation rather than the product, whereas the vendor acknowledged its own onboarding failure and lack of monitoring, and Graham Attwood cited a competing platform preference (Guidewire) and had been leaning toward not renewing.

not_covered: Whether Pinewood served notice by 30 September or its final renewal decision
Whether the Lumen finance director approved the renewal
